Package org.aristonis.diwan.database.eloquent.relations

Class HasMany<R extends Model>

java.lang.Object
org.aristonis.diwan.database.eloquent.relations.Relation<R,HasMany<R>>
org.aristonis.diwan.database.eloquent.relations.HasOneOrMany<R,HasMany<R>>
org.aristonis.diwan.database.eloquent.relations.HasMany<R>
Type Parameters:
R - the related model class
public final class HasMany<R extends Model> extends HasOneOrMany<R,HasMany<R>>
A one-to-many relation whose related rows hold the key, such as a post's comments: Laravel's HasMany.

Declare it on the parent with hasMany(Comment.class). Single use, not safe to share across threads (see Relation).

  • Constructor Details

    • HasMany

      public HasMany(EloquentBuilder<R> query, Model parent, String foreignKey, String localKey)
      Creates the relation. Models normally build it through hasMany(...).
      Parameters:
      query - an unconstrained query on the related model, never null
      parent - the model the relation belongs to, never null
      foreignKey - the related table's column pointing at the parent, bare or qualified, never null
      localKey - the parent's column the foreign key holds, never null
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if an argument is null

    • getResults

      public ModelCollection<R> getResults()
      Returns the related models of the parent. A parent without a local key value runs no query and gets an empty collection.
      Specified by:
      getResults in class Relation<R extends Model,HasMany<R extends Model>>
      Returns:
      the related models in query order, never null

    • one

      public HasOne<R> one()
      Returns a one-result relation on the same columns and parent: Laravel's one(), the way to latestOfMany() and its kin. It is built on this relation's constrained query, so the key condition and every clause recorded here are kept, each once. The two relations share that query, as in Laravel: a join that latestOfMany() adds on the returned relation is also seen when this relation is read afterwards.
      Returns:
      a new relation, never null

    • orWhere

      public final HasMany<R> orWhere(String column, Object value)
      Adds or column = value to the lazy query.
      Parameters:
      column - the column, never null
      value - the value
      Returns:
      this relation
      API Note:
      The relation's own constraints are not grouped, as in Laravel, so an or here widens the result past the parent's rows; group it with where(Consumer).
